name: HA SUSTAINABLE INFRASTRUCTURE CAPI

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The strongest counter to my no_edge is that the engine's 'rich' reading is simply a stale input and, once fixed, HASI is cheap. The engine's 7.9% sustainable ROTCE is the mean of GAAP net income to common for 2023-2025 [$147.8M, $198.5M, $182.6M] divided by equity that has grown to $2.65 billion — a three-year average describing a company that no longer exists, on a business whose managed assets have compounded 20% and whose GAAP ROE is now 20.3%. That is the VLY and ENVA bias in LESSONS.md running on a name whose returns are RISING, and `unstable_rotce` cannot fire because a smoothly compounding series is stable by construction. At my 14% the justified multiple is 2.14 against an actual 1.91, so the gap flips from -44.6% to roughly +12% — from rich to cheap on one corrected input.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Four consecutive quarters of adjusted ROE at or above 15% with the at-the-market programme still dormant, and adjusted earnings per share tracking toward the raised $3.55-$3.65 2028 range. The sharper single test is the investment margin: portfolio yield less cost of debt, which management says is widening, disclosed quarterly.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The earnings improvement is visible and verified in the company's own release. What is NOT visible, and is what stops me, is that the sign of this verdict is set by the cost of equity rather than by the business. The engine's 7.6% comes from a beta of 0.48 with an R-squared of 0.075 — comfortably inside the band LESSONS.md says manufactures false buys, and here it does exactly that on my corrected ROTCE: a LOW cost of equity inflates the justified multiple. HASI is a levered specialty finance company whose assets are long-duration renewable infrastructure; a defensible beta is nearer 1.1-1.3, giving a cost of equity around 11%. At 11.1% my same 14% ROTCE justifies 1.32x against an actual 1.91 — a gap of about -31%, i.e. rich. The sign of the answer flips entirely on a regression that explains 7.5% of the variance.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Two things. First, I could not decompose the $179 million of equity-method income into cash distributions received versus HLBV mark-ups, which is the difference between a 20.3% GAAP return that is real and one that is an accounting artifact — the JXN problem in this file. Second, I did not open the June and July financing 8-Ks (Items 1.01, 1.02, 2.03), so I cannot confirm the current cost and maturity profile of the debt that the entire investment-margin argument rests on.

what_changed: The Q2 2026 release (8-K filed 2026-08-06, EX-99.1) and the 10-Q filed 2026-08-07, both read. GAAP earnings per share $0.92 against $0.74; adjusted earnings per share $0.75 against $0.60, with year-to-date adjusted EPS growth of 24%. GAAP net income to controlling stockholders $129 million against $98 million, driven by $121 million of total revenue plus $179 million of income from equity method investments, less $111 million of expenses and $57 million of tax. GAAP ROE 20.3%, adjusted ROE 15.2%. Managed assets $17.6 billion (+20%); portfolio $8.2 billion; portfolio yield 9.2% from 8.2%; management fees and retained interest income $13 million against $9 million. Guidance RAISED for 2028 adjusted EPS to $3.55-$3.65 from $3.50-$3.60. Also two financing 8-Ks (2026-06-26 and 2026-07-20, Items 1.01/1.02/2.03) that I did not open in detail. No company-specific news in the 90-day store: the name did not move abnormally and did not trade abnormal volume, so absence of news here lowers my confidence that nothing happened rather than confirming it.
consensus_case: HA Sustainable Infrastructure is not a bank and its tangible book is not a capital constraint in the way a bank's is. Managed assets reached $17.6 billion at 30 June 2026, up 20% year over year, against an on-balance-sheet portfolio of only $8.2 billion — the difference is co-investment vehicles and securitised assets that generate management fees and retained-interest income without consuming equity. Portfolio yield rose to 9.2% from 8.2%. The company reported a GAAP return on equity of 20.3% and an adjusted return on equity of 15.2% in the second quarter, raised 2028 adjusted earnings per share guidance to $3.55-$3.65, and reiterated a target of adjusted ROE above 17% by 2028 — with NO shares issued through the at-the-market programme so far this year, so that return is not being manufactured with equity. Paying 1.91x tangible book for a fee-generating originator compounding managed assets at 20% with improving debt spreads is a growth multiple, not a bank multiple, and the market is applying it deliberately.
base_case_rationale: Not applicable — book method. My sustainable ROTCE is 14%, below the company's own 15.2% adjusted return and well below the 20.3% GAAP figure. The discount is deliberate. HASI's GAAP income is dominated by $179 million of equity-method income in a single quarter, which is HLBV accounting on renewable tax-equity positions — economic, but lumpy and partly non-cash, and not a return I will capitalise at face value. Adjusted ROE is management-defined. And the entire business model is levered to two things outside its control: the spread between its cost of debt and portfolio yield, and the durability of the federal renewable tax-credit regime that creates the assets it finances. Fourteen percent is a return comfortably above any honest cost of equity for this business and materially below what is being printed in a good year.
key_risks: The verdict's sign flips on the cost of equity: +12% at the engine's 7.6% (beta 0.48, R-squared 0.075) and roughly -31% at a defensible 11%, and the schema has no field to override it
GAAP return is dominated by equity-method income ($179 million in one quarter) that I could not split between cash distributions and HLBV marks
The business is a spread business into an expected Fed hike on 16 September; management's guidance raise is explicitly credited to improving debt spreads
Federal renewable tax-credit policy is the origination funnel and is outside the company's control
Tangible book is the denominator for a company whose managed assets ($17.6 billion) are more than twice its on-balance-sheet portfolio ($8.2 billion) — the frame may understate the franchise
No company-specific news in the 90-day store, so my confidence that nothing else happened is low
watch_for: Adjusted ROE holding above 15% for four consecutive quarters with the at-the-market programme still dormant
Portfolio yield less cost of debt — the investment margin management credits for the guidance raise
Any resumption of material ATM equity issuance, which would mean the return is being funded rather than earned
Legislative change to the renewable tax-credit regime
